claim: The sentence turns on a verb clause modifying a noun (ははがくれる おかし, "the sweets my mother gives me"), a structure Lesson 15 does not teach.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 3: "person は verb [dictionary form] のが すきです ... By adding the nominalizer の to the dictionary form of the verb". The chapter uses the dictionary form only before の. Card: ははがくれるおかしがすきです, note: "くれる (give to me) sits in front of おかし (sweets) and describes it".
fix: Replace with a くれる sentence in the chapter's own frame (verb dictionary form + のが すきです), or drop the sentence and keep the bare くれる card.

claim: The note states a false rule: a verb that modifies a noun is not always in the dictionary form (past and negative plain forms modify nouns too).
evidence: Card note: "A verb describing a noun is always in the dictionary form." Lesson 15 makes no such claim; its GRAMMAR 2 introduces the dictionary form only as the form listed in dictionaries and the form used before の.
fix: Delete the sentence of the note, or go with the replacement suggested for the same card's untaught-prerequisite finding.

claim: The sentence needs a verb clause modifying a noun (にあう ふく, "clothes that suit me"), which Lesson 15 does not teach; the chapter only puts the dictionary form before の.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 3: "person は verb [dictionary form] のが すきです". Card: にあうふくをかうのがすきです, note: "にあう (suit) sits in front of ふく (clothes) and describes it".
fix: Rebuild the にあう sentence in the のが frame without a noun-modifying clause, or carry にあう on its bare dictionary-form card alone.

claim: The card uses the nominalizer の with は and たのしいです, a frame the chapter never shows; Lesson 15 teaches の only before が (and も in the dialogue) with すきです or じょうずです.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 3: "verb [dictionary form] のが すきです ... Likewise ... のが じょうずです"; Target Dialogue: かくのも すきです. Card: にほんごのアニメがわかるのはたのしいです, note: "here it takes は instead of が".
fix: Recast in the taught frame (e.g. にほんごの アニメを みるのが すきです) or move the のは〜たのしい sentence to the lesson that teaches it.

claim: The English answers for Chan-san as "he", but the book draws Chan as a woman, and this unit's own Chan cards say "She".
evidence: Book, EXERCISES II picture 2 (Page_146_Image_0004) labelled チャン shows a woman. Card: scene "answering whether Chan-san likes mecha anime", English "Yes, (he) likes it." Same unit, x15r-chan-coffee-dansu: "She is good at dancing."

claim: The note says the apposition の of いとこの ポール is "the same の as にほんのアニメ", but the book separates apposition の from possession and affiliation.
evidence: Book, Lesson 6 NOTES on インターンの ラジャさん: "This particle の here expresses apposition, not possession or affiliation." Card note: "This の joins two nouns: いとこ の ポール, \"Paul, [who is] my cousin.\" It is the same の as にほんのアニメ". The base card no-nominalizer itself keeps the two apart ("the possessive の in Lesson 1, or the apposition の in Lesson 6").
fix: Drop "It is the same の as にほんのアニメ" and say it is the apposition の of Lesson 6's インターンの ラジャさん, still not the nominalizer.

claim: The note implies きく is the dictionary form of the "listen" sense of ききます only, but the same verb has the same dictionary form whatever the sense, including Lesson 9's "ask".
evidence: Book, WORD POWER III picture pairs ききます・きく with no gloss; EXERCISES VII uses おんがくを きく ("listen"). Card note: "きく here is the dictionary form of only the \"listen, hear\" sense, matching this card's gloss."
fix: Say instead that きく is the dictionary form of ききます in both senses, and this card drills the "listen" one used in EXERCISES VII.

claim: A second card for すごい, absorbed from a course, sits beside the book's own すごい! card in the same chapter with a different gloss.
evidence: Book, Target Dialogue vocabulary: "すごい! That's great!" Base card sugoi-great: すごい! / "That's great!". Extras card amazing: すごい / "Amazing!" (addition nihongo-102-2026-08).
fix: Exclude the absorbed card, or fold "Amazing!" into the book card's English.
